# A past change in this repository like your task

An earlier task here asked for something like yours, and its change was committed as b764408430. Use it as a worked example where it applies: names, values and details of your task differ, and your task may need more or less than it did.

## Its task

This is our fork of markdownlint. Add a new built-in rule:

- MD061, alias `heading-max-level`, description "Heading level should not exceed the maximum", tag `headings`.
- One parameter, `maximum`: an integer from 1 to 6, default 6. With the default the rule never reports anything.
- Report every heading (ATX or setext) whose level is greater than `maximum`, on the heading's first line, with the detail "Expected: h<maximum>; Actual: h<level>" (for example "Expected: h3; Actual: h5").

Do it the way the existing rules are done: documentation, README, config schema and the files generated from it, tests and snapshots. `npm test` and `npm run lint` must pass. Commit when you're done.

`npm build-config`, `npm build-docs`, `npm update-snapshots`, `npm test`, `npm lint`

## Mistakes it made

- `sed -i 's/`MD025`, `MD026`, `MD036`, `MD041`, `MD043`$/`MD025`, `MD026`, `MD036`, `MD041`, `MD043`,\n  `MD061`/' README.md && sed -n 183,186p README.md; grep -rn "MD060" style/ test/*.mjs --include=* ` failed: 'plan expected 132 assertions but received 134' 'plan expected 236 assertions but received 238' 'plan expected 159 assertions but received 162' 'plan expected 441 assertions but received 449'. What worked instead: `printf '# Heading 1\n\n## Heading 2\n\n### Heading 3\n\n#### Heading 4\n\n##### Heading 5\n\n###### Heading 6\n' > test/heading-max-level-default.md; npm run update-snapshots >/dev/null 2>&1; npm test`

# A past change in this repository like your task

An earlier task here asked for something like yours, and its change was committed as f8cd493b8d. Use it as a worked example where it applies: names, values and details of your task differ, and your task may need more or less than it did.

## Its task

This is our fork of markdownlint. Rule MD024 (`no-duplicate-heading`) treats `# Install` and `## install` as different headings, but they get the same anchor on GitHub. Add a boolean parameter `ignore_case` to MD024, default `false`: when it is `true`, headings whose text differs only in letter case count as duplicates. It must work together with `siblings_only`. Errors are reported as they are today (on the duplicate heading's line, with its text as the context).

Update the rule's documentation, the config schema and the files generated from it, and the tests, the way other rule parameters are done. `npm test` and `npm run lint` must pass. Commit when you're done.
